sites.siteName: Playford B Power Station Site / Port Augusta (retired coal, ElectraNet grid)

matrix.reason: Available screen footprint is 150 ha against a 5 ha reactor envelope; land status: retired coal (brownfield) — state land; same Port Paterson precinct as Northern station. Tenure, zoning, heritage and indigenous/title constraints still require confirmation.

Federal law is the dominant screen-level blocker: EPBC Act s.140A bars approval for construction/operation of a nuclear power plant and ARPANS Act s.10 bars ARPANSA licensing; the site therefore fails the nuclear licensing entry gate regardless of otherwise attractive physical attributes.
A nuclear project would trigger environmental assessment and public consultation; protected-area, habitat, discharge, cultural heritage and social acceptance issues require field-level review.

Cooling source: Spencer Gulf seawater (via Northern Power Station shared cooling infrastructure corridor). Water availability is marked abundant; the stated reactor cooling pathway is screen-plausible only subject to intake/discharge, thermal and water-rights review.
Grid distance is 0 km. Existing switchyard/grid proximity lowers friction where present; longer distances or isolated/off-grid contexts require new interconnection/load studies.
Population density is marked low and hazards include seismic-low. EPZ, exclusion-area control, security standoff and severe-weather/geotechnical assumptions require project-specific analysis.

Brownfield/repower advantages may include existing land, roads, workforce, water corridors and switchyards, but remediation, legacy liabilities, permit transferability and demolition interfaces require diligence.

Screen logistics are inferred from industrial/port/brownfield status, road/rail/grid proximity and available laydown footprint; oversize transport routes, port handling and construction laydown need route survey.

regionSummary: South Australia has physically attractive sites for the selected reactor, but Australia has a dominant federal statutory prohibition: EPBC Act s.140A prevents approval for nuclear power plant construction/operation [au-epbc-140a], and ARPANS Act s.10 prevents ARPANSA from issuing the required licence [au-arpans-10]. South Australia also adds state-level nuclear-waste/electricity restrictions [au-sa-prohibition]. The screen therefore marks every candidate as fail on Gate B, even where land, cooling, grid or logistics appear favourable.

notes: Screen-level triage only. Rankings use only the supplied corpus/site facts and citation IDs; they do not determine licensability, approvals, investment readiness, landowner consent, final engineering feasibility, or public acceptability.
